newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GOVT SET TO WIN CONFIDENCE VOTE -PARTIES.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GOVT SET TO WIN CONFIDENCE VOTE -PARTIES.

text.p: The Finnish government is set to win a confidence vote next week linked to a draft bill to liberalise shop opening hours, officials of the coalition parties' parliamentary groups said on Thursday.
Plenary debate and voting on the contents of the bill are scheduled for Friday, and the decisive third-reading vote will be held on February 28, a parliament spokesman said.
Officials of the parliamentary groups of the three biggest government parties told Reuters by telephone it was clear that the coalition would win the confidence vote.
Parliament's economic committee on Thursday completed its statement on the opening hours proposal, which will form the base for plenary debate and voting.
In line with an earlier compromise between leaders of the five government parties' parliamentary groups, the committee made significant changes in the original government proposal.

Instead of allowing shops to open every Sunday as proposed by the government, the committee said they will be allowed to open on Sundays in June, July, August and December and on five other Sundays to be defined by the ministry of trade and industry.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen turned the shop liberalisation issue into a vote of confidence after the proposal had suffered a surprise defeat in parliament late last year.
Next Friday's vote will be the fifth in Lipponen's left-right-green coalition since it took office in April 1995.
